title: Brightest Position on Street
summary: A straight street is modeled by a number line with street lamps at specified positions and ranges.
statement: A straight street is modeled by a number line with street lamps at specified positions and ranges. Each lamp lights a segment of the street. Calculate the brightness at each position by counting the number of lamps that light it. Identify the position with the highest brightness; if multiple, choose the smallest position.
constraints: lights has 1 through 100000 [position,radius] pairs with integer coordinates.
A lamp illuminates every integer position in its inclusive interval [position-radius,position+radius].
Return the smallest position having maximum brightness.
hints: Inclusive integer intervals become prefix-sum events at left and right+1.
Sweep event coordinates in order while maintaining brightness; update the answer only on a strict improvement.
Add +1 at position-radius and -1 at position+radius+1; prefix-sum sorted events.
Brightness is constant between events, and the first coordinate of the first strictly best region is the smallest maximizer.
editorial: Brightness is constant between events, and the first coordinate of the first strictly best region is the smallest maximizer.

tests.explanation: Brightness two first occurs at negative one, before the tied region beginning at zero.
Position one is illuminated by both lamps and is uniquely brightest.
